data.narrative:
Westmag is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrowly-filtered peer set lacks sufficient depth for robust median valuation.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using total capital raised as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement. This method implies a valuation of $28M based on the $11M raised. A sensitivity range was constructed by adjusting the step-up multiplier ±15% around this central estimate, yielding a low bound of $23M and a high bound of $32M.

The peer-median method was not applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics subsector—only one direct peer met stage-specific filters, falling below the minimum threshold of three datapoints for reliable triangulation. This analysis therefore rests on a single method, suggesting a valuation range of $23M–$32M with a median point of $28M. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for Westmag's specific market positioning and the absence of corroborating peer data to stress-test this assumption.
